text_fidelity_a:
Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light I commute by bike and I'm obsessed with seeing and being seen at night. I have a 650 lumen TerraLUX TT-5 flashlight (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009WFA4KU/) strapped to my handlebars as my primary light. I added this helmet-mounted light set as redundancy / extra security. I've had it about a month now.

This is a pretty good light. It's fairly bright, and I like that it has amber LED's on both sides of both the front and rear light. This makes you visible from any angle (hence the "360" in the name). Having gotten used to the blinding, virtual daylight of the 650 lumen flashlight on my handlebars, the 250 lumens that this light puts out on max doesn't seem quite bright enough to me. But I could get home safely with this alone if my flashlight were to fail, so it's bright enough.

Things I like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) You can aim the light wherever you need it. It's handy for checking out turns before you've made the turn. And I can now see the display from my bike computer without having to wait for a streetlight! And when I'm off my bike, I can see my lock, into my trunk bag, etc.
2) They increase visibility and therefore safety.
3) You'll probably leave them mounted to your helmet most of the time, so you're less likely to forget them. And if you're locking your bike up somewhere you'll probably take your helmet with you, so you'll automatically take your lights too - less chance of theft.

Things I like about this light in particular:
1) It's one of the brighter ones available.
2) It actively aims LED's in every direction, making you highly visible.
3) It's rechargeable and charges via USB.

Things I don't like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) They add weight to your head / neck.
2) They can get knocked around. I take my bike on the train for a portion of my commute, and when we near my stop I have my helmet on and am ready to get my bike out of the rack to disembark; meanwhile other riders are trying to get to their bikes. I frequently bang one or the other of the lights on the overhand above the bikes while we're all jostling around. Also, when I take my helmet off I feel I have to be more careful about stowing it so the lights don't get knocked about.

Things I don't like about this light in particular:
1) It's surprisingly heavy, and it's unbalanced. The front light is virtually weightless. The rear light, which has the battery pack, is surprisingly heavy. I invested in a very nice, "barely there" helmet that weighs virtually nothing. This light makes it feel like a brick. Obviously it's not that heavy, but it is heavier than I expected. And I don't like that all the weight is to the rear. This is okay when I'm leaning forward in riding position, but when I'm stopped at a light or otherwise upright, the weight is pulling my head back.
2) I find the rubberized button to turn it on / change modes difficult to feel and manipulate while I'm riding. If I don't take the train home, my commute is an hour and 15 minutes. To save battery I have it on low when I'm riding on well-lit streets and switch to high otherwise. I've had this light almost a month and I'm not getting better at feeling / adjusting the light. It takes concentration away from riding while I fiddle with it.
3) The tail light mode is not adjustable. It does this odd, slow fade-in / fade-out and that's it. You can't make it be always on, and you can't make it actually flash.
4) You can't have just the taillight on. Once the headlight's on, you can turn the taillight off independently, but you can't ride with just the taillight.
5) The battery is not replaceable. My flashlight / headlight runs on a replaceable, rechargeable battery, which means I can keep a spare battery in my pouch and be sure I have enough battery to get home. I can also ride with one battery while the other's at home recharging. With this light, if the battery runs out you can't use the light until you get to a USB charger. And it takes a good few hours to recharge, so you can't go riding for the hours it takes to recharge. And the low battery indicator is tucked away at the bottom of the taillight, and is only visible after you've plugged it in to recharge, so that doesn't help. So you'd better keep it charged.
6) You can change the angle of the front light, but only in discrete clicks. Each click is a very small angle of change on the device, but changes where the light hits the road by about 20'. I frequently want the light right in between two of the clicks and I can't put it there.
7) The helmet mounts strike me as odd. The front light slides into it's mount and clicks in place, but it slides in from the bottom. That means the if the clicky thing ever fails the light will slide out. If it slid in from the top gravity would keep it in place. And the rear light presses on with four tabs clicking into four slots. You really have to pull on it to dismount it. Odd.

Hmmm. Looking at this review there are way more things in the "don't like about this light" section than elsewhere, which makes it seem like I don't like this light. That's not true. None of the "don't likes" are show-stoppers. I'm keeping the light and I do like it. They're mostly just areas where I feel like the light could be somewhat better. If you buy this light you'll definitely be seen, you'll see where you're going, and you'll probably be happy you have it. These are just my observations for whatever they may be worth to you.
text_fidelity_b: Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light

text_fidelity_a:
SANYO KATANA SCP 6600 BLUE SPRINT CAMERA CELL PHONE I bought this phone to replace my 2 1/2-year old Samsung Vi660. I've been a big fan of the Samsung line, and thought about buying their comparable version to the Katana (the A900) but the reviews of the Katana's superior battery life won me over. I am not much for the fancy features of cell phones - I just wanted a slimmer phone that had a lower radiation emissions level than the Vi660, a built-in speakerphone, and bluetooth connectivity. After using the phone for a few weeks, here are my impressions so far:

The good:

* Excellent sound quality (in each direction) and none of that "echo" effect I used to get with the Samsung
* Long battery life with many powersaving features
* Beautiful screen, and with web access, is capable of diplaying Google satellite/map info that is just as clear as it is on a PC
* Menu design is very functional, with Favorites and Contacts being directly accessable through the touch of a button
* The "Favorites" button brings up a customizable list of 12 shortcuts, which can be either web addresses or any tool/function/menu item within the phone's own menus (it's like having a programmed navigation button with 12 different options)
* This phone emits the least radiation of any phone in the Sanyo line, and is in the bottom half of the list when compared to other manufacturers (the top being the highest emitters).
* Did you lose your Katana? Send it a specific text message and upon receiving it, the phone will lock itself up, erase its contents, and display a "lost phone" message on the outside screen with the sprint customer service phone number
* The center navigation button links directly to the "Missed Alerts" feature, which keeps a running list of missed voicemails and text messages
* Bluetooth functionality is wonderful. It is easy to make and receive calls from the bluetooth headset, and the sound quality is almost better than that from the in-phone microphone
* The phone has four different types of vibration patterns that you can assign to different types of calls/text messages, and an easily accessable "silence all" feature (no rings, no button beeps, etc) that is ideal for business meetings
* There is a feature on the Katana that allows you to screen calls as the callers are leaving a message
* Menus and Contact information are arranged for easy text-messaging access and message drafting

The bad:

* The VGA camera is not the greatest, and pictures are usually come out with a blueish or orangish cast unless the color balance is adjusted manually beforehand (settings to do this are on the phone)
* Sound quality from the speakerphone is great but the microphone isn't sensitive enough, and my callers frequently complain that I sound too far away
* The only feature I sorely miss from the Samsung phones is their far-superior voice dialing capability, which is second-to-none. The Katana relies on user-recorded tags for its voice recognition capabilities, whereas the Samsung phones just recognized my voice without any prior setup. That functionality also let me dial any phone number by saying the digits; a feature lacking in the Katana. Voice recognition does work, however sometimes you must repeat the name a few times to get it to work. If good voice dialing capabilites are a dealbreaker for you, I'd stick with the Samsung line.
* the charging port on the Katana is on the side of the phone, covered by a rotating rubber insert that is a bit flimsy. This makes it awkward to talk on the phone while it is connected to a charger.
* The volume controls on the side of the phone are on the upper portion of the handset and they are *very* slim, making them a bit hard to use.

The Katana seems to be marketed towards a slightly less business-oriented demographic (it's available in cherry-blossom pink, that should be your first clue), and its features reflect this. This is more of a phone for the casual user who is interested in a stylish phone with good basic functionality, and doesn't need many of the fancier functions of its competitors.

6 MONTH UPDATE: Would I buy it all over again? Maybe, maybe not.
It's been almost 6 months since I bought my Katana, and I have to say, I'm on the fence about it. It isn't a bad phone, it gets STELLAR reception compared to the old Samsung, texting is a snap, and its got a great screen for web browsing. But I've given up a lot of great features on my old Samsung and I don't seem to have gained a whole lot of new ones. I don't ever use the speakerphone because everyone asks if I'm having problems with my connection. I am really missing the ability to digit dial by voice. Talking on the phone with the charger sticking out of the side (especially in the car) is pretty awkward, as is trying to connect the charger when you don't exactly have your hands free. Sprint gives you 2 weeks to make up your mind on the phone, I'd take a look at these issues during that time and try to decide how much of an issue these things really are.
text_fidelity_b: SANYO KATANA SCP 6600 BLUE SPRINT CAMERA CELL PHONE

text_fidelity_a: PHOENIX 99226 Power Pro Olympic Bench I wanted to like this weight bench, and I still use it because of its versatility. Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14 I needed a new pair of waders to replace the ones I ripped to shreds when trimming mangroves in our wetlands. It turns out that the old ones couldn't handle some of the spikes and thorns encountered in our Southwest Florida location. While the leaks did help me cool off when in the water you have to be careful of flesh-eating bacteria down here. If a spike/thorn comes through your pants it will probably lodge in your skin. That is not something that I want to deal with.

For a big guy like me (6'3" and 235 lbs) I was very happy to find that they fit so well. The weak spot tends to be the suspenders which normally don't lock properly or fall apart quickly. The clips on these locked up good and tight so I didn't have to worry about losing my coverage. However whether it's backup for my waders or for the tactical pants I wear with boots tromping around in the wetlands, I have a bright orange pair of Carrhart clip-on suspenders to keep my britches on nice and tight. Some of the surplus military pants that come with suspenders fail immediately.

Two obstacles I always watch out for when chest deep in our brackish water are cottonmouths and alligators. There is a large 12' bull alligator we often see crossing the harbor to forage on our side. While gators are common in these parts and normally don't bother humans, a big one like that can make a nice meal out of me. So I'm constantly searching the water for ripples or other disturbances that might indicate that I have company.

As I was completing my trimming on one section of the shoreline I happened to glance to my right and found a 4' gator floating right next to me. Instinct kicked in and I smacked him on the head with the flat side of my machete. He probably wouldn't cause me any trouble but the big bull could just as well be in the area hunting for his next snack.
They often eat smaller gators but I didn't want him to have to make a choice between the little one and big old me. Perhaps the camouflage worked well enough so that they couldn't see me.
text_fidelity_b: Men Waders Waterproof Chest Waders Bootfoot Chest Wader Light Hunting Fly Fishing Waders for Men with Boots Nylon/PVC Wader Camouflage/Brown 8-14

text_fidelity_a:
POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel Update 2 years: the replacement model still working without any issues. I have recommended this unit many times to other swimmers
************
Update 7 Months: I have swum probably 100 times with this snorkel, and it is the best on the market. After 5 months, I was getting a little mist in the air I was breathing. I found if I removed the rubber valve and cleaned it, this mist was mitigated for 40 laps maybe. Then I would take the valve cover off and clean it again (3 minute process maybe). I emailed Ameo and informed them of my issue. They said the first batch of these had a minor valve issue which was corrected in the next version. They offered to ship me a new snorkel of the new design for free. I have used the new snorkel 10 times maybe, and it is even better than the beta version. My air is completely dry. Great product, fantastic customer service.
************
The Ameo PowerBreather is the best swimming snorkel available. I have had the Finis Swimmer's Snorkel [[ASIN:B004O6ECL4 Swimmer's Snorkel Yellow]] for over a year, and it has improved my swimming endurance, but the Ameo PowerBreather is better.

I am a 39 year old man, I swim 1.5 miles, 3 times a week as 3 of my 5 cardio workouts for a week. A year ago, I decided I wanted to integrate swimming into my cardio routines. I swam on a team in 6th and 7th grade, but that has been more than 20 years ago. I started swimming and found I had 2 major issues.

1) I hated keeping count of my laps.
I purchased a lap counting watch to do it for me [[ASIN:B0031IHMFY Swimovate Pool Mate Watch Speed, Distance and Lap Computer for Swimmers (Black)]]

2) Turning to breath was making my neck sore, and reducing the amount of laps I would complete.

I first looked into a snorkel mask [[ASIN:B00ZSFDCYS Seaview 180° Snorkel Mask for Adults/Youth. Easy-Breathing Full-Face Design. Best Snorkeling Experience with Anti-fog and Anti-leak Technology. Huge Viewing Area! Tubeless Design Prevents Gag Reflex.]], but this said it was not for lap swimming, and would not work well for lap swimming.

I then found the Finis Swimming Snorkel (linked above), which has been great over the last year. With a lap-swimming snorkel (front mounted, not side mounted to keep in place while lap swimming) I have been able to consistently improve the quantity of laps I am swimming and the speed of those laps.

I have now moved to the Ameo PowerBreather. I am one of the first Americans to have this device. I have used it maybe 20 times in 2 months, swimming between 50 and 250 laps per swim.

A comparison of the Ameo PowerBreather to the Finis Snorkel:

Cost:
Finis =$30
Ameo=$150

Breath restriction:
Finis= very little. There is a cap to keep water out during turns [[ASIN:B0028AQLYE Snorkel Dry Top]], but I never purchased it.
Ameo= 30% breath restriction would be my estimation of how it feels, 50% restriction with one side using flip turn "blind cap". More about blind cap assy below. [Update: 3 months ownership: even with this perceived restriction, I can pull in more air. I breathe as hard and fast as I would running. My lungs are getting stronger, and as I use this device I find I have gotten into a similar breathing pattern as I would running; great for cardio.]

Comfort during swimming:
Finis= good, no swim cap necessary, goggles fit easily with this, have to adjust occasionally as tube moves.
Ameo= good, must wear swim cap as adjustment knob pull hair without a cap, goggles have to be adjusted differently as the PowerBreather is close to them by your temples. Does not need any adjustment over time, never moves.

Spit buildup:
Finis= every 40 laps maybe I would have to stop and clean out the Finis snorkel, spit would build up in the bottom and backwash a little when I was breathing.
Ameo= no spit buildup, no adjustment. I have swam 250 laps without adjusting the Ameo PowerBreather.

Flip Turns:
Finis= description says you can do flip-turns just blow out hard to clear water from the turn, but when I did them the Finis snorkel would change angle and I would have to adjust it, so no flip turns for me. The freestyle version that follows your head may be better at this.
Ameo=slow flip turns are great, no movement of the device, once you are back at the top of the water, breath normally, no hard exhale needed to clear. Fast flip turns seem to pull in a little water, you can stop this by putting the "blind cap" on your flip turn side (right for me). This blocks off one of your tubes completely, no water in on the flip turn, but now I would say the breathing restriction is 50% up from 30% with both tubes open.

Mouth fit:
Finis= I bit the mouthpiece enough times to bite off the small teeth separator parts, still works, but Finis requires jaw pressure to keep in place.
Ameo= completely held in place by the mechanism. Much more comfortable to not have to hold in place with your mouth.

I am liking the Ameo Power breather much better. If you are dedicated to swimming, I highly recommend it. If you are put off by the price though of $100, then maybe the $30 Finis will get you most of the benefit for a much lower price. Your fitness tools can drive your performance, if you want the best, pay the premium and buy the Powerbreather.
text_fidelity_b: POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel

ESEE Lite Machete Micarta Handles and Sheath This is by far the best machete I have owned and used during my 33 years living in Southwest Florida. I am a big knife collector and ran across this machete by chance when researching other big knives. Previously I had used several Cold Steel machetes which were quite satisfactory--until I discovered and started using the Esee Lite Machete.

Yes, the price point is higher, but what you get is a long, well-balanced, razor sharp, light weight, and flexible blade that cuts through 3" to 5" limbs like the proverbial "knife through butter". Besides that, all Esee products are guaranteed for life. While I haven't abused one to the breaking point yet--although I've tried--all you have to do is send it back to the company for repair or replacement (at the option of the company).

I take two of them into the wetlands with me when cutting Brazilian Pepper trees. Sharpening them is simple with the proper stone and they hold their edge far longer than lesser machetes made of softer steel. You can use them for hours with minimal fatigue because of the good grip, fine balance and light weight. The only better knife that I can compare it to is my Busse Nuclear Fusion Battle Mistress which costs upwards of $500.00. However, the NFBM is considerably heavier and has a thicker blade. This causes shallower cuts and quicker arm fatigue.

So ante up a few extra bucks and enjoy the superior cutting power of the Esee Machete. You will never buy another cheap machete because you will be spoiled by your new Esee.

NOTE 02/15/15: I finally found a drawback to the Esee Lite. The areas I work in are so thick that if you drop the machete or put it down and forget where you put it, it's almost impossible to find. text_fidelity_a:
Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs After reading the pros and cons of fork-mounting vs upright (wheel-mount) I decided to go with these, figuring the mostly aluminum structure would last a while and the fork-mounting would secure the bikes well. I've used the product one time on a short trip, but so far it seems sturdy and the bikes are locked on firmly. My one concern, which I knew in advance of purchase, is that the fork mount only holds the traditional thin skewers/axles. That works fine for our family fleet of tourers and hybrids from years 1998 through about 2012. However, a lot of new bikes now have the much fatter through-axles (particularly bikes w/ disc brakes). So if i get a new bike I'll probably need a new rack.

Vehicle: 2016 Subaru Outback

Pros:
-My big Cannondale Adventure 400 and my wife's Giant Sedona fit perfectly and are secured with front quick release and included rear hold-down strap.
-Reasonable price, though not as inexpensive as some all-steel models out there.
-No tools required, no customization needed for our Outback with factory folding roof rack.
-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.
text_fidelity_b: Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine We took delivery three weeks ago. Relatively easy to set up, but be aware that the seat likes to slide to the end of the stops. Now that we are used to it, my wife and I use it every day, sometimes multiple times a day. We don't put it away, just leave it in place next to the wall, facing the TV.
My main issue is that it, like all the other rowers I've seen, sits too low for someone who (like me) is 76 and 250lbs, with bad knees. At first, I'd either fall the last three inches, hopefully onto the seat, or need some sort of support to get on and off. I solved that problem by wrapping an old belt around the body (see pic), which I could use as a grab bar to lower myself on and lift myself off. If Sunny would put a grab handle on the front, that would be a big help, and save on belts.
A secondary issue is the LCD display. Others have complained that it's not bright enough. The real problem is that it's at the wrong angle. I repurposed a chunk of plastic foam packing to lift the bottom enough to make it clearly visible when seated. Sunny could duplicate that with a simple folding frame.
I should also note that the labeling on the display is wrong. Label says: Time, Count, Total Count, Calories. Actual is: Time, Count, Calories, Total Count.
Finally, I note that almost all of the self-help videos on rowing emphasize managing your strokes per minute. The display doesn't show that. I'd be willing to give up both Total Count and Calories to get that in the display. After all, Total Count is only useful if you are the only person using the machine, and Calories are pretty much a meaningless guess without information like body weight.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine

Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue I looked at tons of weighted hoola hoops on Amazon and saw many of them has some not so great reviews because they were no sturdy or would break apart. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Bad Blood Dreadnaught Folder Knife, G10 Handle, Plain, Black BB0118K My knife collection is kind of eclectic. I prefer big, heavy, sturdy, "do it all" knives, but I also buy unique and unusual blades. Anything from a Busse Gladius to Rob Dalton OTF automatics. I enjoy handing an odd knife to a friend and watching them puzzle out how to open the darn thing (safely). Well-made but unusual knives don't typically sell well so they tend to appreciate over time.

I knew that I had a hit on my hands when I picked up the box holding this Bad Blood Dreadnaught folder. It was hefty in that satisfying way that tells you to expect to find something substantial inside when you open it up. And it was just what I expected. If it were a dog, I would name it something like "Chunk" or "Tank". The over-sized grip has finger grooves cut into it that fit my hands perfectly. The blade is a big chunk of steel that looks like it can handle any task easily. The flipper makes (one-handed) deployment swift and smooth and the blade locks up tight immediately. There is just a little (tiny) bid of blade play when it's locked -- so tiny that it hardly bears mentioning. Right out of the box the blade passes the paper test. Be careful!

This is my first Bad Blood knife and it has impressed me enough (at only $21.96) that I plan to keep my eyes open for any new models. Yes, it's made in China but obviously to exacting standards. The design, materials, and construction resemble that of a knife costing in excess of $100.00. I can hardly believe the value you get for only $21.96. I never thought that I would spend such a reasonable amount of money to add a knife to my collection. Get one (or two) while you can.
text_fidelity_b: Bad Blood Dreadnaught Folder Knife, G10 Handle, Plain, Black BB0118K

Opened the box, pulled the bag containing the bed out of the box and took a deep breath - is this going to work for me? Read the instructions, laid the mattress out where I wanted it, plugged it in and turned the pump handle clockwise. Wow! Three minutes for complete inflation - how cool is that?!? Somewhere I'd read to let the bed "rest" for a few hours to allow any air pockets to work themselves out. I did that and when it was time for me to lay down for the night, it had been about three hours. I added sheets, a blanket and my pillow, laid down and slept so well because it feels just like a regular mattress! None of that weird squeaky noise when you move around on a regular air mattress and the best part is getting up off the mattress. It is 20 inches tall and the edges are sturdy, just like a regular mattress. I'm older and trying to get up off the floor is difficult at best. This mattress, I had no problems stand up. I guess the only downside would be for tall people - I'm 5' 4" and this mattress is perfect for me. I think a 6' man might find it a bit short and harder to get off of, but that is my only thought for a downside on this mattress. Me, I love it!

August 2018 - Addition to this review. My original bed began losing air the beginning of this month. I contacted King Koil and they were quick to get back with me sending a UPS tracking number for my replacement bed! I can't say enough good things about them - they honored their warranty, they were FAST to get the replacement shipped and called me to ensure that I received the replacement and that it was working fine. Again I tell you - pass by the cheap-o air mattresses and buy King Koil. The mattress AND the company are worth it!

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black This lock is exactly what I need, but the lock I received from Amazon today had a cylinder that operates very difficultly. Kryptonite says the lock is a new design, and I wonder if they have all the bugs out yet. At one point the key would only go in half-way and I could see that the back layers of the cylinder were out of line with the outer layers. I don't know how many layers there are, but since the key would only go in half-way there was no way to turn the back layers so they would line up with the outer layers. Finally, after turning the key back and forth very gently for about ten minutes the layers lined up and the key would go in all the way. Unfortunately, the key continued to meet resistance as it turned in the cylinder and I had to ask Amazon for a replacement.

I would not trust the lock I received to operate properly away from home. I have several other Kryptonite locks and the keys all turn very freely in the cylinders. I wonder if I got a bad lock or if Kryptonite is going to have problems with this new design.

Update:

Looking at the lock further, I realized the black housing that rotates to cover the keyhole was also operating very difficultly. As I tuned the housing I saw fibrous plastic shavings visible under the edge of the housing around the keyhole. I removed several shavings with tweezers, and as I turned the cover back and forth more shavings worked their way out around the keyhole. As I pulled them out the keyhole cover began to rotate more easily. All of the shavings in the attached photo came from under the keyhole cover of the lock! If any of the shavings found their way down into the cylinder while the lock was being assembled, or when it was bounced around during shipping, that could explain why the cylinder is difficult to turn and the layers of the cylinder sometimes get out of line with each other as the key is inserted or removed from the lock.

Further Update:

Today, while waiting for Amazon's replacement lock to arrive, I looked again at the lock. Looking at the keyhole with a strong flashlight it appears the design of the metal body of the lock includes a narrow split that extends from the keyhole toward the black plastic end of the lock. I can't see how far the split extends, but I can guess that if it has sharp edges, and if the rotating black keyhole cover is shaped too tightly around the lock body, or if the keyhole cover has an uneven underside, the action of rotating the cover back and forth to uncover and recover the keyhole could actually cause the sharp edges of the split in the lock body to make the shavings I found. If any of the shavings work their way into the cylinder that, in turn, could cause the difficult cylinder operation I encountered.

Final Update:

One comment asked if the replacement lock had the same problem - it did not! I am happy with the replacement lock and so far it has worked fine.
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Evolution LITE Mini-6 11mm U-Lock Bicycle Lock , Black

text_fidelity_a:
Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel I bought two of these and both were non-functional, out of the box.

On the first one, the included line was tangled around inside the mechanism. I had to take it apart and unravel about 6 feet of line that was all caught up in the case. It's hard to explain, but it was basically wedged between the outer casing and the internal components, not just in the spool itself.

On the second one, the casting button was completely unseated on one side. The button has two small pegs which pivot inside of holes in the steel case. I had to take the bottom of the case off, bend the steel tabs that hold the pegs in place, reseat the button and bend the tabs back.

Both work great now and all the components seem pretty good, but this company has some serious quality control issues with assembly. It is pretty ridiculous that 2 out of 2 that I ordered were DOA, still sealed in the undamaged factory box. Luckily, I knew how to fix them, but most people who aren't mechanically inclined or perhaps know very little about reels would have had to return both of them. That is really unacceptable.

Still, they are great little reels now and they would be 5 star if not for the time I had to spend on fixing them. If you have some tools and are confident about taking things apart, I wouldn't hesitate to buy one. If not, well, you might be rolling the dice.
text_fidelity_b: Zebco 11 Micro Fishing Fishing Reel

text_fidelity_a:
Pedallon USB Rechargable LED 100 Lumens Front Bike Light I purchased both lamps, the front (white light) and rear (red light). The rear red would a very good rear lamp except the amount of light emitted to each side (of both front and rear lamps) is very close to zero so they are effectively seen only from the front and rear -- not the sides.

The front lamp has no conventional lens with which to focus and amplify the light so it spreads a very wide beam when mounted horizontally or a very tall beam when mounted vertically. Essentially, it casts light to places you don't need to see. The front beam casts only to about four or five feet. I have a very inexpensive single-LED lamp (two AA batteries) that has a focusing lens which casts a directed a beam that is a little brighter and casts a few feet longer.

The lithium-ion batteries charge with a conventional mini-USB cable. A cable is included but no AC adapter is included. They require 2 hours to charge. That it is rechargeable is not much advantage. At the highest intensity the batteries last less than two hours. Most modest LED lamps using convention AA or AAA batteries will last in excess of 40 hours or more. On an overnight trip or a bicycle tour a conventional AA powered lamp would be a far better choice.

The manual states that "the battery may become ineffective at about 80% of its value after 300 to 500 charge/discharge cycles ... 5 years life span under good care." 300 charges sounds closer to 1- to -2 years in my cycling universe. The manual further states that the battery "loses 1% of its charge per day when stored at room temperature and 5% per day at temps over 104F degrees. Stored battery life decreases 50% at freezing and further degrades as temperatures decrease."

The white front lamp is perhaps better used for other purposes, a dark closet or cupboard, for example. I returned the red lamp but will keep the front lamp for a cupboard. Now that I have it for that other use it will still see some limited use on my bicycle but next time I will make another choice for my cycling needs.
text_fidelity_b: Pedallon USB Rechargable LED 100 Lumens Front Bike Light

SecurityIng® Waterproof 3 Modes 600 Lumes Mini LED Bicyle Light Bright Headlight Lighting Lamp with 4.2V Rechargeable Battery Pack for Camping, Cycling, Riding It took a long time for me to find the right light on amazon, this one fit my criteria well.
1. this is compact
2. it doesn't have a huge battery that will get in the way.
3. It is bright. Im not positive about the 1200 Lumens, but it is as bright as my 900 lumen NR.
4. It is light weight. nothing like my other light,
5. I wanted an actual mount, not a rubber band.

I was skeptical about this light because of the following reasons:
-The name seems suspect. - not a name brand i recognized
- other reviews stated they had problems
-the mount looks super trashy and bulky

After getting the super mini light, I found it to be well made, and it came with a more compact mount than the one picture on amazon. if you go to the sucurityING website, the correct mount is shown. The light output is amazing. the light gives you a lot of down and side light, as well as distance lighting spot beam. it was well appreciated on the trail last night. It has a nice metal housing, and big button in back for high, low, and high-flash. which is really bright, and i don't see using that ever. The charger seems to be of low quality, but it works. my only ride so far has been an hour on high beam.

The only complaints i have are as follows:
1. the battery cable comes detached at the connector with vibration. I had to tie the connector together, and this problem was resolved. make sure you fasten these together, because there is nothing like going down a trail at night when your light goes out. luckily i was on a straight section of trail.
2. The mount takes a bit of getting used to, make sure it is really tight, otherwise it will move. it is hard to get real tight because of the weird mounting clip, vs screw. it worked though in the end. I would have preferred a twist tighten mount.

Overall, this is a great little light for the money. I am happy with my purchase, but cannot say anything about durability as of yet. i would recommend this and other SecurityING products.

text_fidelity_a:
Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft) What I meant by the catchy headline is that this is about the minimum horsepower for the small boat application. In my case I have it hooked to a Sun Dolphin 8.5 play boat. My calculation was that more power was not only not needed, but not wanted. I need those lower speeds for trolling and such. Also I need to make sure that when I go out I can get back in, less paddle.

Here is the deal. The thing is NOT a power hog. As of this writing (super rainy wet year) I have battled winds and currents in our overflowing rivers and having to stay on it all the time has been the test. I haven't got back to the pull out with less than a half battery yet.

My notion is that if you have a 14ft boat or less this engine is adequate. No need to break the bank if you're on a budget. For my purposes it is perfect!

The gadget that tilts the thing. Over the years I have fought with those releases. Not so on the MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor. Smoothest one I have ever seen.

The one thing that is not perfect is the reverse. Don't plan on running it from the front of the boat in reverse. Ain't happening. I don't know if the blades aren't pitched right or what, but the reverse really froths the water without giving much ooomph. I mean, it will back you out of the shallows, but it's not for full time use. Forward, on the other hand works just like you like.

About the handle.... Well, I wound up putting my trolling motor in the back and I was kinda worried about steering. You know, twisting around and all. But with the extension handle which you can pull out a lot or a little....it ended up being zero problem. I think I might actually like it more better on the aft now.

And one heads up. If you plan on putting a transducer onto the foot...be advised, it probably won't fit as the foot is too short. However...my workaround was to put my transducer all the way to the rear against the fin and shim it with some rubber pads on an edge so that I got it near to vertical. And my depth finder works just fine. So no harm done. You could use most anything that won't rot. Your wife's Tupperware, for instance.

I like my MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor a LOT and you will too. If your boat be smaller grab one. You'll be thankin' me!
text_fidelity_b: Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft)

GoSports 2 Person Premium Snow Sled with Double Walled Construction, Pull Strap and Padded Seat - Choose Between Red and Blue Amazon keeps asking me to review this but it hasn't snowed yet! I'm going to give you my first impressions though because this is an awesome sled!

I was shocked when I opened it and realized how sturdy this sled is. While I can't attest to its sleddy-ness I can say that this thing is legit. It's not your average plastic sled, that's for sure. I live in a very cold climate where we can get lots of snow so we have plenty of experience with sleds.

This one is worth every penny for a few reasons. If you don't live in a cold climate it might not make much sense to spend this much on something that you might only use for fun. However, this sled has the potential to be very utilitarian because of how sturdy and heavy duty it is.

You could use this to bring groceries in from the car, if you laid down something to protect the seat, you could use it for firewood, you could use it to move just about anything around you need in the snow because of how large it is and how thick the plastic is. I like that it's smaller than our toboggin that we have for the snowmobiles but it's not so small that you can't use it for something other than sledding. Plus, it's easy to move around manually. Some utilitarian sleds are really only good when pulled by a snowmobile or a 4 wheeler which is great when you need them but sometimes you just need to have something you can move around by yourself.
text_fidelity_b: GoSports 2 Person Premium Snow Sled with Double Walled Construction, Pull Strap and Padded Seat - Choose Between Red and Blue

Wrist Wraps 2 Wraps for Weight Lifting Wrist Support Cotton Wraps Gym Bandage Straps for Men & Women Premium Quality & PRO Rubber I purchased these grips after getting tired all of my other pairs getting stretched out to their limits after a short period of time.. I was hoping these would stand the test of time. Even rogue wraps gave in after a month of 2-3 times a week wearing! It so happened I hurt my wrists after a strenuous lengthy workouts and was looking for a solid support at all costs.I came across of Grip Power Pads and after reading the reviews decided to give them a try and here is what I found:
Pros: they are very sturdy, they stretch but not too much, hence keeping the shape longer. They are long enough to wrap around your wrist and provide strong support to the wrists.
Cons: The loops around the thumb stretch out too fast and loosen up way too fast.. they don't have much support for holding the wrist wrap in place, so overall I don't see much point in using them in the way they are. Even putting both loops around thumb doesn't create enough stability to keep the wrap in place.. so what I do, I just adjust the wraps each time I have to lift or pull-up and once done - I release them.
Overall the wraps are perfect except for the weak thumb loops support but I'd buy them just for the stability of the wrist and overall durability.
Update 09/2017: Disclamer: For reviewing the grips company sent me another pair for free, and to my surprise!!! New pair of grips had a nice quality thumb loops, made of the same material as a wrist grip! Super quality in everything now..No complaints at all! After wearing the grips for six months now, quality is still the same, not a significant stretch of a grip, still going strong! Now I'm considering buying them in all colors! Rogue wrist grips are long resting in a garbage can while these keep on living! Thank you for the quality at affordable price!

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak eddy Glass Water Bottle, 24oz I am SO HAPPY that they finally made a glass Camelbak!! I have it in blue but will be getting it in every color because I'm so excited they finally gave me what I wanted. For a couple of years now I had been using a kerplunk glass bottle and just placing the camelbak top/straw on it. But it didn't fit quite right. This bottle is great. There's no plasticy or metal taste to the water. Glass is the only material that doesn't leach a seperate taste to the water after it's been in there for a while. The only thing is that the straw is still plastic. I actually have some straws made out of glass that I sometimes use with the camelbaks, and they work, but again- there is a fit issue so I often can't use them. I wish camelbak would make a stainless steel version of their straw.

UPDATE/ March 2013: for those who are interested, I found a company that makes custom sized glass straws. It's called "GLASS DHARMA" and they have a website. If you order their "smoothie" sized straws and ask that they be custom cut to 7 & 3/8 inches, they will fit great with these camelbaks. I've been using their glass straws for years and they are really durable- last forever if you don't drop them on a hard floor (they are glass after-all), but this is the first time I realized they did custom sizes so I measured and ordered a couple and they fit/work great! Their straws come with a life-time guarantee. I even dropped my camelbak on the floor once and luckily it didn't break, but I lifted the lid and checked the glass straw to make sure it was fine- not a scratch. If you decide to use these you should wet the glass straw and inside of the camelbak lid before twisting the straw in- The lubrication will make it slide in without you having to worry about being too rough. The straws hold up perfectly inside these camelbaks. (Oh- and since they are glass I wouldn't use them in bottles that you use for sports activities or anything like that.) They look cooler than the plastic straws too because you can see the cloudy white plastic straw through the bottle vs the crystal-clear glass straw that matches better with the bottle (and the water).

I still use the plastic straw when I leave the house so that I don't have to worry about breakage during transport etc... but when I drink indoors (which is 99% of the time for me) I use these glass straws instead. The plastic straw is ok- unlike when I use plastic bottles which give off a plasticy taste almost immediately- the straw only seems to leech a plasticy taste if it's been sitting in the water for a couple of days or more... but Still I like to avoid plastic whenever possible and if you are like me you might appreciate this alternative too.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak eddy Glass Water Bottle, 24oz

text_fidelity_a:
NcStar 1" High Ring with Weaver (RB13) I used these to mount a 50mm whitetail scope on a .308 FAL. The clearance is not enough to also use the peep sight, but that's because the scope is 50mm -- a 40mm scope would have allowed me to still use the peeps.

We've put about 100 rounds downrange on two different outings after zeroing and the scope has held zero fine, so I know the rings aren't moving despite the .308 recoil.

Some people think these rings aren't solid enough but I feel they are great. Just make sure you tighten the hex screws and the mounting nuts tightly, AND make sure your rail mount is also tight. Check the fasteners periodically if you're using a high-recoil rifle.

Only complaint I have is that the hex screw sockets (the part the hex wrench fits into) aren't sturdy enough to really hold up to a lot of cranking. I noticed one of the screw sockets started rounding out and it became more and more difficult to screw or unscrew with the included wrench. If I ever have to take this scope off, I won't be surprised if have to replace one or more hex screws.

Still, a good quality product for the price and I give it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: NcStar 1" High Ring with Weaver (RB13)

text_fidelity_a: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black Alas, dear friends, I admit....... somewhat reluctantly of course........ that i found the assembly of the "Mirrycle" somewhat of a challenge and never actually arrived at that happy moment I had dreamed of -- riding contentedly on my road bike and being able to cast a glance down at my "Mirrycle" to see if some danger was lurking behind as I peddled my beloved bicycle through the wicked city streets.  This thing has not been machined as well as one would hope.  Despite my heroic efforts, I just could not get the first screw into it's intended spot on Mirrycle's extension piece because the threads on the screw do not seem to match up with the interior threads cut into the plastic 'tapped hole' on the plastic extension that screws to the mirror.  I found that I had to expend a Herculian effort just to get the first screw into the hole.  And, while I'm not an engineer, auto mechanic or strangely gifted with screwdrivers, I do consider myself competent enough to use one.  Maybe if I had hands as big as bear paws, I could have forced it...but alas...I do not possess such paws.  SO.... I went in search of my old standby, WD40, to loosen the screw which was - at this point, hopeless stuck in the hole.  --Only after applying more WD40  was I able to complete the task of getting the first poorly machined part together.  To my surprise, they fit well or seemed to --as that was as far as I got in this overachiever's nightmare. Because, as we 'lovers of WD40" know, all too well, it drips terribly and makes everything that you didn't want to slide, very slippery. So, what I had thought was going to be a pleasant hour spent putting on my new bike mirror started to twist and turn into something else....a maddening morning cavorting down the road of imbecilic incompetence!  I had unintentionally involved myself in someone's diabolic effort to create havoc in our Republic by using the simplest of methods: assembling a plastic mirror!  Still - I was not to be defeated! I carefully  wiped the small, smooth pieces of plastic down, NOT ONCE, NOT TWICE...but THRICE! No, nothing could stop me from getting this wretched product together at this point, even if I was still in my pajamas.  BUT, little did I know I faced an even more diabolical obstacle because the second screw presented me with the identical problem.  And, yes, I had to repeat the application of WD40 again.  It was almost too much to bear, but then I remembered!  "I'm not a mere mortal, I'm a cyclist! I can bike 100 miles a week! And everyone else who reviewed this thing on Amazon LOVES IT!"  Tragically, I was not victorious in my quest to fully assemble my nifty Mirrcyle MTB Bar End Mountain Bike Mirrow, because at the quintessential moment when it seemed like victory was within my grasp -in when the second screw was about to be turned into place, ....tragedy struck!  The whole slippery mess  slipped  -  literally - from my grasp and went crashing to the wooden floor in my kitchen and the glass mirror cracked into many pieces........... taking with it all my hopes and dreams of having a mirror that actually functions on my road bike.  I was as shattered as my broken Mirrycle and slumped over the couch in defeat.  I did order another mirror - but decided that I'm just going to do without one for now.  I haven't wanted to waste precious riding time wrestling with it.  If I do, I'll update.  Cheers and happy riding!
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror , Black

text_fidelity_a: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow) This water bottle has some definite pros and cons. Lets start with the good: for sure it's great to be able to drink fruit infused water! I don't drink any sodas or sugary drinks, so this is a great idea. The bottle is also very pretty (i got the yellow) and it's really awesome to see my yellow top with my yellow lemon slices in the bottle. It's also nice that the fruit is contained in the inner tube and not able to come out when poured. There is also a nice flip top with a handle so it can be clipped onto a bag or just carried by the little top handle. Thats about all the good points. The unfortunate problem with this bottle is that it doesn't allow you to drink all the water in the bottle! Because of where the holes are to let water in, it prevents you from finishing your last 2 inches of water. So thats a problem because if i want to finish my water i have to take the whole top off and then the wet tube with the fruit drips everywhere and it's just awkward. You also cant fill the bottle with water all the way up because the tube of fruit displaces so much of the water. Then on top of it, when you have drank about half of the bottle, the water isn't even touching the fruit anymore! Plus, when you go to drink it, it's hard to get any water out because the fruit from the tube bumps up against the water hole and blocks it. The water will come out but only a little bit, it's very obstructed. Then we have the problem of the flip top itself. It does seal well, however in order to open the top to drink it, you have to pinch your finger under this brittle plastic piece to open it. I feel like it's very difficult to open and hurts my finger. I also feel like it's so brittle its only a matter of time before it breaks. So, overall I don't see myself continuing to use this bottle. It doesn't hold much water and doesn't function very well. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for a review and I always give my honest opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow)

Fwosi Kukri Blade -13-Inch Heavy Duty Fixed Blade Knife Gorkha or Military Kukri with Carbon Steel Blades, Bone & Wood Handle - Handcrafted in Nepal This is truly a stunning set of knives, and the Kukri knife will be the largest in my collection thus far. Both knives arrived oiled with the blades sharp. Each knife also has a drilled hole near the handle end for a lanyard if desired. Both of these are full tang knives and share a heavy duty sheath each having its own fitted sleeve/sheath. I had a hard time at first getting them in and out of the sheaths because of how tight they were, but the sheaths do start to loosen up as you remove the knifes and insert them back into the sheaths. The larger knife weighs 1 lb, 11 oz. The smaller knife weighs 7.3 oz. Both knives with the sheath have a combined weight of 2 lb, 10 oz. The sheath fits over a belt, and the belt strap is quite wide and looks to me like it should fit over most belt widths. At first I thought the sheath for the smaller knife could be detached by perhaps a snap or velcro, but the smaller knife sheath is strongly attached to the large sheath.

The only issue I found was along the outer edge of the smaller knife handle where the blade runs through the handle. The metal wasn't fully smooth and had what felt like microscopic burrs along the edge. I was able to smooth this with a super fine nail file, but had to be very careful in doing so such that I would not sand any of the wood on the handle. This only took me about a minute to do, but had to be done.

Aside from the little issue mentioned above which I was able to easily fix, I really love this set. Both knifes and sheaths are super strong, heavy duty and well-constructed. Great addition to any knife collection!
